![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8fc551f1439ed5a551ae8fd18234479bb062d43ae9e4faf55d896739f76e0f4d.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{4/z}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
question.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 4,\,\,1\le y\le \frac{4}{z},\,\,0\le x\le 4-yz\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9a59198b60398e2b3044296c3cc76b4748785303029dccc1087320cd11cb7d55.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 4,\,\,1\le y\le \frac{4}{z}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\frac{4}{z}\,⟹\,z=\frac{4}{y}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,\,1\le z\le \frac{4}{y}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9bc88aa4f0ad07d89ff5dd3c0de16208cb8bf47d774b557a7bf2140790c95291.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{4/y}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$
